definitions.explanation: Pain in a tooth or teeth. The Sino-Japanese ({音読|おんよ}み) reading; the same kanji are also read {歯痛|はいた} in everyday speech.

examples.japanese: {歯痛|しつう}で{夜|よる}も{眠|ねむ}れなかった。
examples.english: I couldn't sleep at night because of a toothache.

examples.japanese: {歯痛|しつう}が{続|つづ}いたので、{我慢|がまん}せずに{歯医者|はいしゃ}に{行|い}った。
examples.english: The toothache persisted, so I went to the dentist instead of putting up with it.

notes:
{歯痛|しつう} is the Sino-Japanese ({音読|おんよ}み) reading for tooth pain. In casual speech the same kanji are often read {歯痛|はいた}, or people simply say {歯|は}が{痛|いた}い (my tooth hurts).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {歯痛|しつう}がする: to have a toothache
- {歯痛|しつう}を{抑|おさ}える: to relieve tooth pain
- {歯痛|しつう}{止|ど}め: painkiller for toothache

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {歯|は}が{痛|いた}い: my tooth hurts — the everyday spoken phrasing
